newsitem.title: USA: Conn. budget surplus projected at $292 mln - report.
newsitem.headline: Conn. budget surplus projected at $292 mln - report.

text.p: The nonpartisan Office of Fiscal Analysis projected that Connecticut's budget surplus this year will be surprisingly high at $292 million, Hartford Courant reported Tuesday.
This is about $70 million higher than the figure projected two months ago, and is also higher than an estimate by Gov. John Rowland.
Given the bigger surplus, state lawmakers now say they have more leeway for a tax cut, the Courant said.
Legislators are still debating the size and mix of the cuts, with decisions expected before the legislative session's end on June 4.
The main reason for the surplus is that the economy has remained stronger than initially expected, and the stock market has continued to boom after some volatile periods.
Up to $166 million of the surplus might be used to pay off the state's debt, the report said. This would free up other money that would have been used for debt payments if the surplus had been lower.
Without the surplus, Connecticut would have needed to find $166 million from projected spending or tax cuts to make the debt payments.
